Impact: high – F-033 is the only gate failure and fails in both original and rebuild; keyboard users cannot reach rows, and axe reports 0 violations so it would go unnoticed. (ux)

What to change: When porting, do not copy the rebuild's TaskRow as is: its outer div has role="none" and the focusable button is nested inside, so the row check still fails. Make the row itself (or the listbox option) the focus target with tabIndex, role=option and aria-selected, and add keyboard activation.

Was, now and should

speed

Was (original)

The original served raw, uncompressed assets: bytes 219742 (score.json speed.bytes original) with no content-encoding in golden/network.har. LCP was 48 ms and INP 32 ms; heap 2.3 MB; build 813 ms. Its search input cost 13.1 ms per key at 4x CPU slowdown (script-ms-per-key original), the one slow input (other inputs 2.4-4.0 ms per the skeptic note). Cause: moment 2.31.0 plus an unused zustand (technology.md).

Now (rebuild)

The rebuild transfers 66044 bytes (bytes rebuild), but the skeptic note shows this is mostly gzip: raw JS is 163250 bytes, so the real size cut is about 20-25%, not the 70% in the delta of 0.6994. LCP is worse: 976 ms against 48 ms (lcp delta -0.9508), stable over 10 runs (952-976 ms), and the skeptic agrees it is real. INP is 24 ms against 32; script per key is 4.2 ms against 13.1 ms; heap 2.4 against 2.3 MB; build 881 against 813 ms; CLS 0.0001 against 0. The speed delta is 0.0611.

Should

Keep the rebuild's cheaper input handling (debounce plus AbortController, stack.md) and the removal of moment. Then find out why LCP is about 20 times slower (page paints late, possibly the loading skeleton or the fetch before first content) and fix that; it is the user-visible regression. Serve both with the same compression before comparing bytes again. Not measured: real network speed, different CPUs, runs beyond Chromium.

ux

Was (original)

The original has weak loading, error and empty states and no focus handling: judges scored it 3 on the guideline walk-through (score/gaps.json j0-0, cite B/source/src/App.jsx:51; j1-0, cite src/components/TaskForm.jsx:10). It has silent add failure (golden/screens/add-failed-silent), stale search responses (search-stale-response), an unvalidated settings save (settings-invalid-email-saved), and rows not keyboard operable (F-033). Probe failures: 10 of 22 (probe-failures original).

Now (rebuild)

The rebuild scored 7-8 from the same judges on the same question (cite SettingsForm.tsx:54); judged ux delta 0.4667 (judges 0.5, 0.4, 0.5). It adds role="alert" and role="status" messages (TaskDetail.tsx:103, SettingsForm.tsx:124-161, AddTaskForm.tsx:78-81), cancelling of older searches, and validation. Rows are still not focusable (F-033). The measured probe-failures shows 40 against 10 (delta -0.75), but the skeptic found this is the same "root" screen captured ten times (root, root-2 to root-10, golden-rebuild/screens); deduplicated it is 4 layout-shift failures against 10. The overall ux delta of -0.1417 is therefore pulled down by a counting artefact, not by a real worse experience.

Should

Rebuild's approach is better. Fix F-033 by making the row itself the focus target or by giving the container a listbox role with the button/option as the child, and move `tabIndex`/focus there. Remove the 4 layout shifts (reserve space). The probe count should be deduplicated by screen name before it is used. Not measured: dark mode and narrow-width screenshots beyond the 1440 light captures in golden/screens, real screen-reader output, other browsers (score.json notChecked).

simplicity

Was (original)

Small and plain: 325 lines, 15 files, 6 dependencies, 2 build steps, longest file 79 lines (score.json simplicity measured). Plain JavaScript with React, Vite, moment and an unused zustand (technology.md). The simplicity is partly missing code: no validation, routing or tests.

Now (rebuild)

3614 lines, 26 files, 11 dependencies, 2 build steps, longest file 813 lines (lines, files, dependencies, build-steps, longest-file). The skeptic notes about 1070 of those lines are tests and README, and the longest file is the e2e spec project/tests/e2e/tracker.spec.ts; app source alone is 2358 lines, about 7x. TypeScript, Vitest and Playwright are added (stack.md). Judges: -0.2, -0.4, -0.3; simplicity delta -0.419.

Should

Neither side. The original is too thin to fix the defects, but the rebuild is larger than the problem needs. Keep the no-router, no-state-library, built-in http choices; consider splitting the 813-line spec and the 641-line styles.css, and check that Playwright plus Vitest are both needed for a single-screen app. Count tests apart from app code in the scorer. Not measured: time for a newcomer to get started, maintenance cost over time.

compatibility

Was (original)

a11y-violations: 10 (axe nodes) in the original: no `<main>`, an unlabeled `<select id="status">`, skipped heading levels (score.json compatibility note; golden/screens/*/a11y.json). overflow-narrow: 0.

Now (rebuild)

a11y-violations: 0 on all 10 rebuild screens; the render has `<main>`, aria-label="Status" and h1/h2/h3 (delta 1, skeptic agrees). overflow-narrow: 0 in both (delta 0). Compatibility delta 0.5. No judged scores (judged count 0).

Should

Keep the rebuild's markup. The remaining gap is F-033 (focusable rows), which axe does not catch since it found 0 violations, so the zero number overstates keyboard access. Not measured: browsers other than Chromium (score.json notChecked), older browsers (Intl, fetch/AbortController use), touch devices, high-contrast mode.
